title: "Yet (Saith the Lord) If David's Race
description: "Yet (Saith the Lord) If David's Race in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 89, part 6, headed “The covenant of grace unchangeable; or, Afflictions without rejection”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "Yet (saith the Lord) if Da-vid's race, "The child-ren of my Son, "Should break my laws, a-buse my grace, "And tempt mine an-ger down;

lines: "Should break my laws, abuse my grace,
"Their sins I'll visit with the rod,
"But I'll not cease to be their God,
"Once have I sworn (I need no more)
"The sun shall see his offspring rise
"Long as he travels round the skies
"Sure as the moon that rules the night
"Till the fix'd laws of shade and light

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
